history.dynasty: Parashurama tradition; renovated by Sakthan Thampuran (Rama Varma, 1790-1805)
history.period: Ancient (tradition says among the oldest of Kerala's 108 Shiva temples; one source claims ~1300 years - UNVERIFIED)
history.summary: Vadakkunnathan Temple, set atop Thekkinkadu Maidan in the centre of Thrissur's Swaraj Round, is dedicated to Shiva as Sri Vadakkunnathan ('Lord of the North'). Tradition holds it was established by Parashurama and ranks first among the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala. Its Shiva lingam is covered by a great mound of ghee from centuries of neyyabhishekam. Adi Shankaracharya's parents, Aryamba and Shivaguru, are traditionally said to have prayed here for a child. Rama Varma Sakthan Thampuran (1751-1805), the Cochin ruler around whom modern Thrissur developed, renovated the temple with its four gopurams and founded the Thrissur Pooram festival centred on it. The complex also houses shrines to Parvati, Rama, Krishna, Ganapathi and Shankaranarayana.

name: Vadakkunnathan Temple
town_description: Thrissur is a major city in central Kerala, often called the cultural capital of the state for its temples, pooram festivals and classical arts. The Vadakkunnathan Temple sits at its heart on Thekkinkadu Maidan, encircled by the Swaraj Round. Guruvayur, one of Kerala's most important pilgrimage centres, lies about 25-27 km away.

travel.road: On Swaraj Round in the city centre; well connected by bus and road across Kerala

visitor_information.best_time: Early morning on weekdays; October-March; Thrissur Pooram season (April-May) for the festival spectacle
visitor_information.opening_hours: 4:00 AM - 11:00 AM and 5:00 PM - 8:30 PM (verify - sources vary: one says 4-10 AM / 5-8:20 PM; a visitor review says 6 AM-12 PM / 5-8 PM). Traditional dress code enforced; photography prohibited inside.
